```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(flextable)
library(ftExtra)
library(dplyr)

# Source all data prep and model results
source("analyses.R")

### Table helpers ###

set_flextable_defaults(font.family = "Calibri", font.size = 9,
                       padding.top = 3, padding.bottom = 3,
                       border.color = "black")

# Column alignment given as one letter per column (e.g. lrlr)
align_columns <- function(ft, spec) {
  key  <- c(l = "left", r = "right", c = "center")
  cols <- strsplit(spec, "")[[1]]
  for (a in unique(cols)) ft <- align(ft, j = which(cols == a), align = key[[a]], part = "all")
  ft
}

# Journal-style table
base_table <- function(df, spec) {
  ft <- flextable(df)
  ft <- theme_booktabs(ft)
  ft <- colformat_md(ft)
  ft <- align_columns(ft, spec)
  ft <- valign(ft, valign = "bottom", part = "header")
  set_table_properties(ft, layout = "autofit",
                       width = if (knitr::is_html_output()) 0.6 else 1)
}

# Write the numbered title (same style as figures), then the table
finish_table <- function(ft, title) {
  title_block(title)
  flextable_to_rmd(ft)
}

# Order of tables and figures, numbered within each kind
OUTPUTS <- c(
  demographics = "Table",
  en_models = "Table",
  en_importance = "Figure",
  sfc_em = "Figure",
  lme = "Table",
  motion = "Supplementary Table",
  criteria = "Supplementary Table",  # Comparison of superaging criteria (not in this file but used for table numbering)
  flow = "Supplementary Figure",
  en_features = "Supplementary Table",
  en_svm = "Supplementary Table",
  en_svm_importance = "Supplementary Figure",
  lme_change = "Supplementary Table",
  atlas_comparison = "Supplementary Figure"
)

# Start figure numbering at 2 and supplementary tables at 2
FIRST_NUMBER <- c(Figure = 2, `Supplementary Table` = 2)

# Numbered label for text and captions
ref <- function(key) {
  kind <- OUTPUTS[[key]]
  first <- if (kind %in% names(FIRST_NUMBER)) FIRST_NUMBER[[kind]] else 1
  number <- match(key, names(OUTPUTS)[OUTPUTS == kind]) + first - 1
  paste0(kind, " ", number)
}

# Title
caption_title <- function(key, text) sprintf("**%s.** %s", ref(key), text)

# Absolute path so images render in both HTML and Word
FIG_DIR <- normalizePath("figures")

# Title above any table or figure
title_block <- function(title) cat("\n\n::: {.fig-title}\n", title, "\n:::\n\n", sep = "")

# Numbered title above a figure
fig_title <- function(key, text) title_block(caption_title(key, text))

# One centered image
single_figure <- function(file, width) {
  cat(sprintf("\n\n::: {.fig-single}\n![](%s){width=%s}\n:::\n\n", file.path(FIG_DIR, file), width))
}

# Italicize heading rows and indent the rest by level
style_rows <- function(ft, labels, is_heading, level) {
  ft <- compose(ft, i = which(is_heading), j = 1, value = as_paragraph(as_i(labels[is_heading])))
  for (l in 1:3) ft <- padding(ft, i = which(level == l), j = 1, padding.left = 18 * l)
  ft
}

# Table whose heading rows have empty data cells (from the Python table scripts)
render_sectioned_table <- function(df, spec, title) {
  is_heading <- df[[2]] == ""
  ft <- style_rows(base_table(df, spec), df[[1]], is_heading, ifelse(is_heading, 0, 1))
  for (i in which(is_heading)) ft <- merge_h_range(ft, i = i, j1 = 1, j2 = ncol(df))
  finish_table(ft, title)
}

### Formatting helpers ###

# β coefficient
fmt_b <- function(x) formatC(as.numeric(x$coef), format = "f", digits = 4)

# 95% CI as "lo to hi" for inline text
fmt_ci_text <- function(x) {
  ci <- as.numeric(x$ci)
  paste0(formatC(ci[1], format = "f", digits = 4), " to ",
         formatC(ci[2], format = "f", digits = 4))
}

# 95% CI as "lo-hi" for table cells
fmt_ci_dash <- function(x) {
  ci <- as.numeric(x$ci)
  sep <- if (ci[2] < 0) "- " else "-"  # Space stops markdown turning "--" into an en dash
  paste0(formatC(ci[1], format = "f", digits = 4), sep,
         formatC(ci[2], format = "f", digits = 4))
}

# "Coef (lo-hi)" combined cell for tables
fmt_coef_ci <- function(x) paste0(fmt_b(x), " (", fmt_ci_dash(x), ")")

# p-value for inline text: returns "=0.0450" or "<0.0001"
fmt_p <- function(p, digits = 4) {
  p <- as.numeric(p)[1]
  if (is.na(p))       return("=NA")
  if (p < 10^-digits) return(paste0("<", formatC(10^-digits, format = "f", digits = digits)))
  paste0("=", formatC(p, format = "f", digits = digits))
}

# p-value for table cells, with significance stars
fmt_p_star <- function(p, digits = 4) {
  p <- as.numeric(p)[1]
  if (is.na(p)) return("")
  base <- formatC(p, format = "f", digits = digits)
  if      (p < 0.001) paste0(base, "***")
  else if (p < 0.01)  paste0(base, "**")
  else if (p < 0.05)  paste0(base, "*")
  else                base
}

# FDR p-value for inline text
fmt_p_fdr <- function(x) fmt_p(x$p_fdr)

# Inline stats for one LME model
fmt_stats <- function(x) {
  paste0("β=", fmt_b(x), ", 95% CI ", fmt_ci_text(x), ", p", fmt_p(x$p_value), ", pFDR", fmt_p_fdr(x),
         ", marginal r²=", fmt_r2m(x), ", conditional r²=", fmt_r2c(x))
}

# Marginal / conditional R² from LME models
fmt_r2m <- function(x) formatC(as.numeric(x$marginal_r2),    format = "f", digits = 4)
fmt_r2c <- function(x) formatC(as.numeric(x$conditional_r2), format = "f", digits = 4)

# Results for one model ("elastic_net", "linear_svm"), connectivity type ("SFC", "FC", "SC") and feature set ("t1", "t1_slope")
en <- function(type, features, model = "elastic_net") {
  en_models[en_models$model == model & en_models$connectivity_type == type & en_models$features == features, ]
}

# Elastic net vs SVM feature importance agreement for one feature set ("t1", "t1_slope")
agreement <- function(features) en_svm_agreement[en_svm_agreement$features == features, ]

# Inline stats for one elastic net model
fmt_auc <- function(x) {
  f3 <- function(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = 3)
  paste0("AUC=", f3(x$auc), ", 95% CI ", f3(x$ci_low), " to ", f3(x$ci_high),
         ", p", fmt_p(x$p_value, 3), ", pFDR", fmt_p(x$p_fdr, 3))
}

### Derived demographic stats ###

# Look up a cell from the demographics table (built by demographics_table.py)
demo_cell <- function(variable, column, section = "") {
  demographics_table[[column]][demographics_table$Variable == variable & demographics_table$Section == section]
}

# Demographics table p-value formatted for inline text
demo_p <- function(variable, section = "") {
  p <- demo_cell(variable, "p_value", section)
  if (startsWith(p, "<")) p else paste0("=", p)
}

pct_sa <- round(as.numeric(demo_cell("N", "Superager")) / as.numeric(demo_cell("N", "Whole cohort")) * 100, 1)
### Derived model stats ###

# Main atlas results
res <- lme_results[[MAIN_ATLAS]]

# Schaefer 400 results
res_s400 <- lme_results$schaefer400

# Min p-value or pFDR across networks, excluding any reported separately
min_stat <- function(fits, stat, exclude = character(0)) {
  min(sapply(fits[setdiff(names(fits), exclude)], `[[`, stat), na.rm = TRUE)
}

# SFC change minimums across both atlases (Schaefer 200 SN reported separately as nominally significant)
min_sfc_slope_p <- min(min_stat(res$group_change, "p_value"), min_stat(res_s400$group_change, "p_value"))
min_sfc_slope_p_fdr <- min(min_stat(res$group_change, "p_fdr"), min_stat(res_s400$group_change, "p_fdr"))
min_ravlt_slope_p <- min(min_stat(res$memory_change, "p_value", exclude = "salience"), min_stat(res_s400$memory_change, "p_value"))
min_ravlt_slope_p_fdr <- min(min_stat(res$memory_change, "p_fdr", exclude = "salience"), min_stat(res_s400$memory_change, "p_fdr"))

fmt_round2 <- function(p) formatC(round(p, 2), format = "f", digits = 2)
```

Our overall cohort included `r demo_cell("N", "Whole cohort")` participants: `r demo_cell("Female, n (%)", "Whole cohort")` female participants with a mean (range) baseline age of `r demo_cell("Age", "Whole cohort range", "Baseline")` years. `r pct_sa`% of the cohort met longitudinal superager criteria (see `r ref("flow")` for further details). Superagers and typical older adults did not vary on age at baseline (p`r demo_p("Age", "Baseline")`) or follow-up (p`r demo_p("Age", "Follow-up")`), years of education (p`r demo_p("Education (years)")`), baseline MMSE scores (p`r demo_p("MMSE", "Baseline")`), or follow-up duration (p`r demo_p("Follow-up duration (years)", "Follow-up")`). However, superagers were more likely to be female (p`r demo_p("Female, n (%)")`) and had higher MMSE scores at follow-up (p`r demo_p("MMSE", "Follow-up")`). These demographic statistics as well as statistics regarding the tests used to define superagers are summarized in `r ref("demographics")`.

```{r table1, results='asis'}
n_row <- demographics_table[demographics_table$Variable == "N", ]
demo <- demographics_table[demographics_table$Variable != "N", ]

# Headings are the only rows with no data
is_heading <- demo$`Whole cohort` == ""
is_section <- is_heading & demo$Variable == demo$Section
# Rows below a subsection heading (e.g. cognition) sit one level deeper
in_subsection <- ave(as.integer(is_heading & !is_section), demo$Section, FUN = cumsum) > 0
level <- ifelse(demo$Section == "" | is_section, 0, ifelse(is_heading | !in_subsection, 1, 2))

tbl1 <- demo[c("Variable", "Whole cohort", "Non-superager", "Superager", "p_value")]
names(tbl1) <- c("Variable",
                 sprintf("Whole cohort (n=%s)", n_row$`Whole cohort`),
                 sprintf("Typical older adults (n=%s)", n_row$`Non-superager`),
                 sprintf("Superagers (n=%s)", n_row$Superager),
                 "p-value")

ft <- style_rows(base_table(tbl1, "lrrrr"), tbl1$Variable, is_heading, level)
for (i in which(is_heading)) ft <- merge_h_range(ft, i = i, j1 = 1, j2 = ncol(tbl1))
finish_table(ft, caption_title("demographics", "Participant characteristics"))
```

::: {.note}
Values are mean (SD) or n (%).
&dagger;Used to classify superagers; group differences on these measures are expected by design.
Abbreviations: MMSE, Mini-Mental State Examination;
RAVLT, Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test; SD, standard deviation.
:::

**Machine learning models:** We calculated SFC as the correlation between each region's structural connectivity – measured through whole-brain tractography – and functional connectivity – measured as resting-state timeseries correlations (Figure 1; details in Methods). We used SFC, structural connectivity, and functional connectivity as features in separate elastic net classification models predicting superager status. Only SFC significantly predicted superager status in both the baseline (`r fmt_auc(en("SFC", "t1"))`) and baseline plus annual change (`r fmt_auc(en("SFC", "t1_slope"))`) models. Neither the functional connectivity baseline (`r fmt_auc(en("FC", "t1"))`) nor baseline plus annual change (`r fmt_auc(en("FC", "t1_slope"))`) models were significant, nor were the structural connectivity baseline (`r fmt_auc(en("SC", "t1"))`) or baseline plus annual change (`r fmt_auc(en("SC", "t1_slope"))`) models (`r ref("en_models")`). The top SFC features selected by permutation-based feature importance were broadly distributed across networks in both the baseline and baseline plus annual change models (`r ref("en_importance")`; `r ref("en_features")`). We repeated the analyses with a second machine learning model, a linear support vector machine, and found the same pattern: only SFC significantly predicted superager status in both the baseline and baseline plus annual change models (`r ref("en_svm")`). SFC feature importance was also strongly correlated between the two models (`r ref("en_svm_importance")`).

```{r table_en, results='asis'}
CONNECTIVITY_LABELS <- c(SFC = "Structure-function coupling", FC = "Functional connectivity", SC = "Structural connectivity")
FEATURE_LABELS <- c(t1 = "Baseline", t1_slope = "Baseline + annual change")
f3 <- function(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = 3)

# One data row per model ("elastic_net", "linear_svm")
model_row <- function(type, features, model) {
  x <- en(type, features, model)
  list(Model          = FEATURE_LABELS[[features]],
       `AUC (95% CI)` = paste0(f3(x$auc), " (", f3(x$ci_low), "-", f3(x$ci_high), ")"),
       `p-value`      = fmt_p_star(x$p_value, 3),
       pFDR           = fmt_p_star(x$p_fdr, 3),
       Permutations   = as.character(x$n_perm))
}

# Connectivity type heading, then its baseline and annual change rows
model_table <- function(model) {
  bind_rows(lapply(names(CONNECTIVITY_LABELS), function(type) {
    bind_rows(list(Model = CONNECTIVITY_LABELS[[type]], `AUC (95% CI)` = "", `p-value` = "", pFDR = "", Permutations = ""),
              lapply(names(FEATURE_LABELS), model_row, type = type, model = model))
  }))
}

render_sectioned_table(model_table("elastic_net"), "lrrrr", caption_title("en_models", "Elastic net models predicting superager status"))
```

::: {.note}
AUC confidence intervals are DeLong intervals on out-of-fold predictions. p-values are from permutation tests, with FDR correction across the six models.
Permutations show how many shuffled-label models were run before 50 matched or exceeded the model's AUC, indicating non-significance. The maximum number of possible permutations was 1,000.
\* p < 0.05, \*\* p < 0.01, \*\*\* p < 0.001.
Abbreviations: AUC, area under the curve; CI, confidence interval; FDR, false discovery rate.
:::

```{r figure-en-importance, results='asis'}
fig_title("en_importance", "Structure-function coupling feature importance in elastic net models")
single_figure(paste0("feature_importance_brain_", MAIN_ATLAS, ".png"), "80%")
```

::: {.note}
The 20 most important structure-function coupling features in the baseline (A) and baseline plus annual change (B) elastic net models, ranked by permutation importance. Colors indicate the network each feature belongs to. Hashed bars in (B) denote annual change features. Numbers in parentheses indicate the index of each region within its network in the Schaefer atlas. (C) Regions of each network shown on the Schaefer and subcortical atlases.
Abbreviations: LH, left hemisphere; PCC, posterior cingulate cortex; PFC, prefrontal cortex; R, right; RH, right hemisphere.
:::

**Structure-function coupling, superager status, and episodic memory:** We next used repeated-measures linear mixed-effects models to examine whether SFC varied longitudinally by superager status at the global and network levels across two brain parcellations: the Schaefer 200 and Schaefer 400, both with added subcortical regions. With the Schaefer 200 parcellation, superagers showed higher SFC than typical older adults globally (`r fmt_stats(res$group$global)`), in heteromodal regions (`r fmt_stats(res$group$hmod)`), and in memory-relevant networks including the DMN (`r fmt_stats(res$group$dmn)`), ECN (`r fmt_stats(res$group$control)`), and SN (`r fmt_stats(res$group$salience)`). By contrast, SFC in sensory regions did not differ by superager status (p`r fmt_p(res$group$sensory$p_value)`, pFDR`r fmt_p_fdr(res$group$sensory)`).

We found similar results using the Schaefer 400 parcellation. Superagers showed higher SFC than typical older adults in the ECN (`r fmt_stats(res_s400$group$control)`) and SN (`r fmt_stats(res_s400$group$salience)`). We found nominally significant results in heteromodal regions (`r fmt_stats(res_s400$group$hmod)`) and trends globally (`r fmt_stats(res_s400$group$global)`) and in the DMN (`r fmt_stats(res_s400$group$dmn)`). As in the Schaefer 200 parcellation, SFC in sensory regions did not differ by superager status (p`r fmt_p(res_s400$group$sensory$p_value)`, pFDR`r fmt_p_fdr(res_s400$group$sensory)`).

```{r figure-sfc-em, results='asis'}
fig_title("sfc_em", "Structure-function coupling, episodic memory, and superager status analyses")
single_figure(paste0("em_sfc_cortex_plot_", MAIN_ATLAS, ".png"), "100%")
```

::: {.note}
(A) Cortical surface and subcortical plot of the unthresholded mean difference in regional structure-function coupling between superagers and typical older adults in the Schaefer 200 parcellation, averaged across both timepoints. Warm colors indicate higher coupling in superagers; cool colors indicate lower coupling. (B, C) Linear mixed-effects model coefficients and 95% confidence intervals for regional structure-function coupling as a function of superager status (B) and episodic memory (C) in the Schaefer 200 (solid lines) and Schaefer 400 (dotted lines) parcellations. Boxes show pFDR for each parcellation. Filled boxes are significant after FDR correction, outlined boxes are nominally significant (p < 0.05, uncorrected), and gray boxes are not significant. Abbreviations: FDR, false discovery rate; SFC, structure-function coupling; DMN, default mode network; ECN, executive control network; SN, salience network; CI, confidence interval.
:::

We next examined the relationship between global and network level SFC and episodic memory across the cohort longitudinally with linear mixed-effects models. With the Schaefer 200 parcellation, higher SFC was associated with better episodic memory globally (`r fmt_stats(res$memory$global)`) and in heteromodal regions (`r fmt_stats(res$memory$hmod)`). We found nominally significant results in the DMN (`r fmt_stats(res$memory$dmn)`) and the ECN (`r fmt_stats(res$memory$control)`). The SN showed a trend (`r fmt_stats(res$memory$salience)`). SFC in sensory regions was not associated with episodic memory (p`r fmt_p(res$memory$sensory$p_value)`, pFDR`r fmt_p_fdr(res$memory$sensory)`).

With the Schaefer 400 parcellation, we found that higher SFC was associated with better episodic memory globally (`r fmt_stats(res_s400$memory$global)`), in heteromodal regions (`r fmt_stats(res_s400$memory$hmod)`), the DMN (`r fmt_stats(res_s400$memory$dmn)`), the SN (`r fmt_stats(res_s400$memory$salience)`), and the ECN (`r fmt_stats(res_s400$memory$control)`). SFC in sensory regions was not associated with episodic memory (p`r fmt_p(res_s400$memory$sensory$p_value)`, pFDR`r fmt_p_fdr(res_s400$memory$sensory)`). `r ref("lme")` summarizes these results. `r ref("sfc_em")`A presents the difference in regional SFC between superagers and typical older adults averaged across baseline and follow-up, with warmer colors indicating higher SFC in superagers (see `r ref("atlas_comparison")` for a comparison with both parcellations). `r ref("sfc_em")`B and `r sub("Figure ", "", ref("sfc_em"))`C display these results by parcellation.

We next examined whether global and network level SFC change – modeled as an interaction with time in linear mixed-effects models – differed by superager status or was associated with episodic memory. We found no evidence that superager status was associated with SFC change in any network across either parcellation (ps ≥ `r fmt_round2(min_sfc_slope_p)`, pFDRs ≥ `r fmt_round2(min_sfc_slope_p_fdr)`). In the Schaefer 200 parcellation, SFC change in the SN was associated with episodic memory, but this did not survive correction for multiple comparisons (`r fmt_stats(res$memory_change$salience)`). SFC change in other networks was not associated with episodic memory in either parcellation (ps ≥ `r fmt_round2(min_ravlt_slope_p)`, pFDRs ≥ `r fmt_round2(min_ravlt_slope_p_fdr)`). `r ref("lme_change")` summarizes these results.

```{r table2, results='asis'}
# Helpers to build data rows for LME models
lme_row <- function(region, model) {
  list(
    Region                 = region,
    `Coefficient (95% CI)` = fmt_coef_ci(model),
    `p-value`              = fmt_p_star(as.numeric(model$p_value)[1]),
    pFDR                   = fmt_p_star(model$p_fdr),
    `Marginal r²`     = fmt_r2m(model),
    `Conditional r²`  = fmt_r2c(model)
  )
}

# Section header row (spans all columns via merge_at below)
hdr_row <- function(label) {
  list(Region = label, `Coefficient (95% CI)` = "",
       `p-value` = "", pFDR = "",
       `Marginal r²` = "", `Conditional r²` = "")
}

# Section type row (model description label, styled differently from hdr_row)
type_row <- function(label) {
  list(Region = label, `Coefficient (95% CI)` = "",
       `p-value` = "", pFDR = "",
       `Marginal r²` = "", `Conditional r²` = "")
}

NETWORK_LABELS <- c(
  global = "Global SFC", hmod = "Heteromodal SFC", dmn = "DMN SFC",
  control = "ECN SFC", salience = "SN SFC", sensory = "Sensory SFC"
)

type_labels <- c(
  "Repeated measures linear mixed-effects analyses",
  "Repeated measures linear mixed-effects analyses — change"
)

ATLAS_LABELS <- c(schaefer200 = "Schaefer 200", schaefer400 = "Schaefer 400")

# Outcome header, then one block of network rows per atlas
lme_section <- function(res_by_atlas, model, header, suffix = "") {
  bind_rows(
    hdr_row(header),
    bind_rows(Map(function(res, atlas) {
      fits <- res[[model]]
      bind_rows(
        hdr_row(ATLAS_LABELS[[atlas]]),
        bind_rows(Map(function(fit, net) lme_row(paste0(NETWORK_LABELS[[net]], suffix), fit), fits, names(fits)))
      )
    }, res_by_atlas, names(res_by_atlas)))
  )
}

# Main effects (change = FALSE) or SFC change (change = TRUE) for both atlases
lme_table <- function(res_by_atlas, change = FALSE) {
  if (change) {
    bind_rows(
      type_row(type_labels[2]),
      lme_section(res_by_atlas, "group_change", "Superager status", " × time"),
      lme_section(res_by_atlas, "memory_change", "Episodic memory", " × time")
    )
  } else {
    bind_rows(
      type_row(type_labels[1]),
      lme_section(res_by_atlas, "group", "Superager status"),
      lme_section(res_by_atlas, "memory", "Episodic memory")
    )
  }
}

# Headings italic and full width: outcome, then atlas, then indented network rows
render_lme_table <- function(tbl, title) {
  is_heading <- tbl$`Coefficient (95% CI)` == ""
  level <- ifelse(tbl$Region %in% type_labels, 0,
           ifelse(tbl$Region %in% ATLAS_LABELS, 2,
           ifelse(is_heading, 1, 3)))
  ft <- style_rows(base_table(tbl, "lrrrrr"), tbl$Region, is_heading, level)
  for (i in which(is_heading)) ft <- merge_h_range(ft, i = i, j1 = 1, j2 = ncol(tbl))
  finish_table(ft, title)
}

render_lme_table(lme_table(lme_results[ATLASES]), caption_title("lme", "Associations between structure-function coupling, superager status, and episodic memory"))
```

::: {.note}
Models adjust for time, baseline age, sex, and years of education, with a random intercept per participant.
\* p < 0.05, \*\* p < 0.01, \*\*\* p < 0.001.
Abbreviations: CI, confidence interval; DMN, default mode network; ECN, executive control network;
FDR, false discovery rate; SFC, structure-function coupling; SN, salience network.
:::

## Supplementary material

### Functional magnetic resonance imaging motion

We excluded 33 participants for excessive head motion (more than 30% of volumes exceeding 0.5 mm framewise displacement). Superagers and typical older adults did not differ significantly in mean framewise displacement or volumes scrubbed at baseline or follow-up (`r ref("motion")`).

```{r table_motion, results='asis'}
render_sectioned_table(motion_table, "lrrrr", caption_title("motion", "Motion during functional magnetic resonance imaging"))
```

::: {.note}
Values are mean (SD). p-values are from Welch t-tests.
Abbreviations: fMRI, functional magnetic resonance imaging; SD, standard deviation.
:::

```{r figure-flow, results='asis'}
fig_title("flow", "Superager classification at baseline and follow-up")

```

::: {.note}
Participants were classified as superagers only if they met both the memory and non-memory criteria at
baseline and at follow-up; all other participants were classified as typical older adults.
Abbreviations: RAVLT, Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test; TMT-B, Trail Making Test part B.

### Elastic net feature importance

`r ref("en_features")` lists the top-ranked SFC features from the elastic net models alongside their ranks in the elastic net and linear support vector machine models.

```{r table_en_features, results='asis'}
en_title <- caption_title("en_features", "Top structure-function coupling features from the elastic net models")
if (is.null(en_features_table)) {
  title_block(en_title)
  cat("*Table pending.*\n\n")  # Placeholder until the CSV is generated
} else {
  render_sectioned_table(en_features_table, "lrrr", en_title)
}
```

::: {.note}
Features are ordered by elastic net feature importance (ΔAUC). Ranks are out of all `r agreement("t1")$n_features` baseline or `r agreement("t1_slope")$n_features` baseline plus annual change SFC features.
Abbreviations: AUC, area under the curve; L, left; LH, left hemisphere; PCC, posterior cingulate cortex; PFC, prefrontal cortex; R, right; RH, right hemisphere; SFC, structure-function coupling; SVM, support vector machine.
:::

### Linear support vector machine models

```{r table_svm, results='asis'}
render_sectioned_table(model_table("linear_svm"), "lrrrr", caption_title("en_svm", "Linear support vector machine models predicting superager status"))
```

::: {.note}
AUC confidence intervals are DeLong intervals on out-of-fold predictions. p-values are from permutation tests, with FDR correction across the six models.
Permutations show how many shuffled-label models were run before 50 matched or exceeded the model's AUC, indicating non-significance. The maximum number of possible permutations was 1,000.
\* p < 0.05, \*\* p < 0.01, \*\*\* p < 0.001.
Abbreviations: AUC, area under the curve; CI, confidence interval; FDR, false discovery rate.
:::

SFC feature importance was strongly correlated between the elastic net and linear support vector machine models in both the baseline (Spearman ρ=`r fmt_round2(agreement("t1")$spearman_rho)`) and baseline plus annual change (Spearman ρ=`r fmt_round2(agreement("t1_slope")$spearman_rho)`) models (`r ref("en_svm_importance")`). Of the `r agreement("t1")$top_n` most important SFC features in each model, `r agreement("t1")$top_n_shared` were shared in the baseline model and `r agreement("t1_slope")$top_n_shared` in the baseline plus annual change model.

```{r figure-en-svm-importance, results='asis'}
fig_title("en_svm_importance", "SFC feature importance in the elastic net and linear support vector machine models")
single_figure(paste0("en_svm_importance_", MAIN_ATLAS, ".png"), "100%")
```

::: {.note}
Each point is one SFC feature, colored by network. Filled points are baseline features and open points are annual change features. The dashed line marks equal importance in both models. Labels show the five most important features in the elastic net model, with parcel numbers in parentheses.
Abbreviations: AUC, area under the curve; LH, left hemisphere; RH, right hemisphere; SFC, structure-function coupling; SVM, support vector machine.
:::

```{r table_s1, results='asis'}
render_lme_table(lme_table(lme_results[ATLASES], change = TRUE), caption_title("lme_change", "Associations between structure-function coupling change, superager status, and episodic memory"))
```

::: {.note}
Models adjust for time, baseline age, sex, and years of education, with a random intercept per participant.
\* p < 0.05, \*\* p < 0.01, \*\*\* p < 0.001.
Abbreviations: CI, confidence interval; DMN, default mode network; ECN, executive control network;
FDR, false discovery rate; SFC, structure-function coupling; SN, salience network.
:::

```{r figure-atlas-comparison, results='asis'}
fig_title("atlas_comparison", "Structure-function coupling difference between superagers and typical older adults in the Schaefer 200 and 400 parcellations")
single_figure("sfc_diff_atlas_maps.png", "100%")
```

::: {.note}
Cortical surface and subcortical plots of the unthresholded mean difference in structure-function coupling between superagers and typical older adults, averaged across both timepoints, in the Schaefer 200 (top) and Schaefer 400 (bottom) parcellations. Warm colors indicate higher coupling in superagers; cool colors indicate lower coupling.
:::
